items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: You know, Plas Johnson, Conte Candoli, Oscar Castro-Neves. It was just awesome.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Oh yeah. And I’m like, “Who liked me anyway?” I didn’t know he was going to take it to a record company. I had no clue. And he had talked to Telarc. And he said “you got an audition.” So I did my audition for Telarc and he happened to be playing in Chicago at the Blackstone, Joe Segal’s room, the Jazz Showcase. And so he flew me out to do one night. And basically I sang two tunes and the record company people were there and I was scared half to death. I was just shaking. And it went all right. And he…

You know, Plas Johnson, Conte Candoli, Oscar Castro-Neves. It was just awesome. And I think out of that whole thing one of my favorite moments was when Ray, he came down to San Diego to my house, and we’re sitting at the piano going through some tunes and ideas, and we were going to do “A Train.” And he says well my ex-wife used to do stuff — my ex-wife used to take things, you know, and she’d take it slow and then she would make it fast. And so he says well let’s try this with “A Train.” Because I don’t think…
The percentage of gigs that you get called for these days, are they mostly for your singing or your bass or for both? Now people can get two for one I guess.
